headline: Stocks rebounded Wednesday (S&P 500 +1.31%, Nasdaq +1.60%) on CoreWeave's beat, but Nvidia fell about 6.5% after hours on a report its board is weighing CEO Jensen Huang's future; the 10-year sits near 5% after a hot CPI.
regime: Hiking regime: the Fed funds target is 3.75-4.00% and a December hike is the base case (the only FedWatch figure found this run is 76.3% after the Nov 6 jobs report; no post-CPI reading found). The 10-year is about 5.00% (bonds were closed Nov 11), the VIX about 18.3 and Waller backs a 25bp December hike.

lean.why: Nasdaq-100 futures were about -0.9% and S&P -0.4% early Thursday after Nvidia's after-hours drop; Barr speaks at 10 am ET and Cisco and AMAT report after the close.
PPI (Nov 13; forecast +0.4% headline, +0.3% core per Continuum Economics), Nvidia earnings (Nov 17), FOMC minutes (Nov 18) and PCE (Nov 25) are ahead with a hike expected.
AI demand data is strong (CoreWeave backlog about $132.5B, TSMC October revenue +60%), but a 5% 10-year and a hiking Fed pressure valuations.

rates.n: Per Deutsche Bank via Investing.com, Nov 10; next FOMC Dec 8-9
76.3% per CME FedWatch after the Nov 6 jobs report (Zacks); earlier Investing.com read of ~99% was Nov 10; no newer figure found
5.00% Nov 10 (TheStreet); 4.998% on Yahoo's Nov 11 ticker while bonds were closed
Freddie Mac survey of Nov 5 (older); Nov 12 release not found this run
102.29 on Nov 11 (Reuters via Yahoo); 102.45 per another page; +0.5% Tuesday

$86.27 early Nov 12 (TipRanks); Brent about $92.5; US-Iran de-escalation talks
18.32 on Yahoo's Nov 11 ticker (time of quote not stated); 25.64 on Nov 6 (Zacks)

sectors.why: (Nov 9 read, not updated.) First Solar fell about 5% Monday as oil dropped; higher yields are a headwind for rate-sensitive builders.

(Nov 5-9 read.) Moderna closed Nov 9 at $269.00 on its first profitable quarter in two years; an analyst on TheStreet pointed to rotation toward healthcare and financials Nov 10; Hims & Hers fell 16.6%.
(Nov 4 read, not updated.) Lockheed -7%, L3Harris -6%; industrials slipped 0.08% on Nov 10.
Nasdaq +1.60% Nov 11 on CoreWeave (+24.7% to $60.77); Micron, Sandisk and SK Hynix +10% or more; but Nvidia fell about 6.5% after hours on the CEO report (Yahoo, FinWire).
Financials led Nov 10, up 0.49% (TheStreet); a hiking Fed helps margins but raises credit worries. No bank-specific news was found.
The 10-year at about 4.99% pushes mortgage rates back up from 7.18%; Thursday's Freddie Mac survey is the test.
Gold fell 2.6% to about $4,032 and silver 3.55%; McEwen fell 16.5%.
Energy rose 0.41% on Nov 10 even as WTI settled at $86.04, the lowest since Aug 31; Iran talks drive crude.
The Russell 2000 opened +3.15% but closed -0.68% at 2,821.38; a 5% 10-year hurts borrowers.
(Nov 9 read, not updated.) Tesla rose about 5% Monday on robotaxi expansion (Yahoo).
Utilities fell 0.23% on Nov 10; Constellation closed Nov 9 at $276.09 after a Q3 beat; GE Vernova and Vertiv rose premarket on JPMorgan notes.
(Nov 4 read, not updated.) GEO -6.7% and CoreCivic -5.2% on the new Congress.

news.head: Nvidia falls after-hours as board reportedly weighs CEO Huang's future
news.mean: Nvidia closed Wednesday at $173.73 (+2.9%) then fell about 6.5% after hours to about $162 on a WSJ report that the board is preparing to oust CEO Jensen Huang, with an independent investigation under way; Baird cut it to Neutral. The stock was down about 14% in November. Other sources cited -7% to -8% after hours.
react: Governance and key-person risk before Nov 17 earnings
Fell over 6% in Hong Kong on chip-access scrutiny
Mixed; CoreWeave and memory names rallied Wednesday
news.hist: Rule of thumb: sudden leadership uncertainty at a mega-cap leader tends to widen swings in the stock and its index until the board gives clarity.
news.today: Expect wide NVDA and Nasdaq swings at the open; confirmations or denials from the company would be the catalyst.
news.later: Investors may weigh the Nov 17 earnings report and any board announcement against the AI demand data.

news.head: October CPI runs hot: headline +0.4%, core +0.3%
news.mean: Headline CPI rose 0.4% vs 0.3% expected and core 0.3% vs 0.2% (September headline was +0.6%). Rents rose 0.2%, food 0.5% and energy 0.7%. A year-over-year figure was not published because October 2025 prices were not collected during the shutdown.
react: December hike seen as nearly locked
news.hist: Rule of thumb: a core print above consensus during a hiking cycle tends to push yields up and hurt long-duration stocks the same day.
news.today: Stay small into PPI on Nov 13; yields near 5% are the pressure point.
news.later: Investors tend to watch core inflation trend (core path 0.3, 0.3, 0.3 over Aug-Oct per Stocktitan) and the Dec 8-9 FOMC.

news.head: Fed's Waller backs a December hike, would consider 50bp; Logan sees two more
news.mean: Governor Waller supports at least 25bp in December and would consider 50bp if core CPI was 0.3% or higher. Dallas Fed's Logan said two more hikes are needed. Goldman expects a December and a March hike, peaking at 4.25-4.5% (Saxo).
react: About 99% for December (CME FedWatch via Investing.com)
news.hist: Rule of thumb: officials floating a bigger move right after a hot print raise the odds that markets price a steeper path.
news.today: Fed speakers keep yields in focus; Veterans Day thins bond trading today.
news.later: A hiking cycle is a rate-and-valuation story; investors tend to watch the Dec 8-9 meeting and Nov 18 minutes.

news.head: 10-year Treasury yield back near 5%
news.mean: The 10-year closed about 4.99% (touching 5.00-5.02% intraday) and the 2-year about 4.73%, up roughly 17-18bp. Treasury cash markets are closed Nov 11 for Veterans Day.
news.hist: Rule of thumb: a 10-year yield at or above 5% has tended to weigh on housing, small caps and unprofitable growth first.
news.today: Watch whether 5% holds when bond trading is thin today.
news.later: Investors tend to compare equity valuations with a 5% risk-free rate.

news.head: Nvidia falls 5.47% to $168.89 as board probes CEO reports
news.mean: Independent directors hired Wachtell Lipton to investigate reports about CEO Jensen Huang. The stock fell 4.27% on Nov 9 and 5.47% on Nov 10 to $168.89 on 429.3M shares, about 2.8% above its 52-week low. It rose about 3.5% premarket Nov 11 and reports Nov 17.
react: Tech was the weakest sector Nov 10
news.hist: Rule of thumb: headline-driven drops into earnings can reverse quickly or extend; the earnings call is the next test.
news.today: Premarket bounce vs the $164.27 low; Nov 17 earnings are the next catalyst.
news.later: Investors tend to separate the probe from AI demand data in the Nov 17 report.

news.head: Oil settles at lowest since Aug 31 as Iran tensions ease
news.srcN: Khaleej Times, Nov 9; Eurasia Business News, Nov 11
news.mean: WTI (Dec) settled at $86.04 (-0.93%) and Brent (Jan) at $91.49 (-1.17%), both the lowest settlements since Aug 31. Trump said new Iran attacks are unlikely while talks progress; Brent fell 4.65% on Nov 9. AAA gasoline fell below $4 for the first time since July (Stocktitan).
react: Eases headline pressure if it holds
news.hist: Rule of thumb: falling crude helps fuel-heavy industries and headline inflation with a lag; Hormuz shipping risk can reverse it quickly.
news.today: Brent rebounded to about $91.6-92.2 on Nov 11 after an overnight dip.
news.later: Investors tend to watch Iran talks and shipping risk near Hormuz.

news.head: Gold drops 2.6% to about $4,032 on yields and the dollar
news.srcN: Eurasia Business News, Nov 11; Stocktitan, Nov 10
news.mean: Spot gold fell about 2.6% to roughly $4,032 and silver 3.55% to about $51.41 as yields and the dollar rose. McEwen Mining fell 16.5% (Stocktitan).
news.hist: Rule of thumb: gold tends to weaken when real yields and the dollar rise together.
news.today: Gold readings vary by source ($4,030-$4,055 on Nov 11).
news.later: Investors tend to watch the 10-year yield and hike odds as gold's drivers.

news.head: CoreWeave beats and raises; shares jump premarket
news.mean: CoreWeave closed Wednesday at $60.77, up 24.7%, after raising its revenue outlook and citing about $9B in customer prepayments; it slipped about 5% after hours. The Nasdaq gained 1.60% and memory and photonics names rose 10% or more.
news.hist: Rule of thumb: an AI-infrastructure beat often lifts peers the same day; debt burdens are the recurring caveat.
news.today: Premarket gains can fade at the open; Nebius reports Nov 12.
news.later: Investors tend to weigh backlog growth against $46.9B of debt.

news.head: Anthropic IPO range set at $70-78; chip makers among buyers
news.mean: The range is $70-78 for 825M shares, with a $26B private placement that includes buyers such as Nvidia, AMD, Google and Microsoft. TSMC's board approved up to $500M of Anthropic stock. The listing date is reported as next Thursday (Nov 19) but is not independently confirmed, and TheStreet flags inconsistencies in the proceeds figures.
react: Analysts call it a core driver of the AI trade
news.hist: Rule of thumb: large IPOs can pull money from other growth names around the pricing date.
news.today: Details are still being reported; treat figures as preliminary.
news.later: Investors tend to watch how the IPO prices against the $70-78 range.

news.head: October payrolls +165,000 vs 59,000 expected
news.mean: Payrolls rose 165,000 vs 59,000 expected, unemployment fell to 4.1% from 4.2%, and average hourly earnings rose 3.1% y/y.
react: Adds to the case for a hike
news.hist: Rule of thumb: strong jobs during a hiking cycle tends to support the hawkish case and the dollar.
news.today: Old news today; it is the backdrop for the CPI reaction.
news.later: Investors tend to watch labor data alongside core inflation.

news.head: Mortgage rate fell to 7.18% in the Nov 5 survey, third straight decline
news.mean: Freddie Mac's 30-year rate was 7.18% (prior week 7.24%, a year ago 6.22%) and the 15-year 6.57%. The 10-year has since risen to about 4.99%, so the Nov 12 survey could reverse the decline.
news.hist: Rule of thumb: mortgage rates tend to follow the 10-year yield with a short lag.
news.later: Housing is rate-sensitive; investors tend to watch the 10-year yield.

news.head: Earnings movers: AAON +19%, ZipRecruiter +54%, Hims -17%, Groupon -23%
news.mean: AAON rose 19.3% (Q3 sales +84.1%), PepGen 92.9%, and ZipRecruiter 53.6%. Hims & Hers fell 16.6% on a lower EBITDA outlook, Digital Turbine 35.8% and Groupon 23%.
news.hist: Rule of thumb: big single-day earnings gaps are often followed by high volatility.
news.later: Investors tend to read guidance changes, not only the quarter.

news.head: Costco declares a $30 special dividend
news.mean: The special dividend is $30 per share, about $13.3B in total, with a Nov 24 record date and Dec 4 payment. The stock rose 1.58% after hours (Stocktitan).
news.hist: Rule of thumb: a special dividend usually lowers the share price by about the payout on the ex-date.
news.today: Record date Nov 24; the price adjusts on the ex-date.
news.later: Taxes on special dividends differ from ordinary ones; investors tend to check them.

playbook: Homebuilders, REITs, utilities, small caps and unprofitable growth are pressured first. Banks and the dollar hold up better.
Housing, small caps, growth and gold benefit. Mortgage rates ease a few weeks later.
Gold and miners, emerging markets and big multinationals gain. Importers lose.
Airlines, cruise lines and shippers win. Energy stocks lose. Headline inflation eases.
A growth and small-cap rally is the usual response. Banks lose some margin tailwind.
Bonds rally, defensives (healthcare, staples, utilities) lead. Cyclicals and banks get hit by recession worries.
